title: Convert a `List<Employee>` back into a `List<String>` of CSV rows (reverse of the above).
shortTitle: Convert a List<Employee> back into a List<String> of CSV rows (reverse of the above)
keyPoints: map() can serialise each object into a CSV row by joining its fields with commas
Use BigDecimal.toPlainString() for salary to avoid scientific notation on very large numbers
Serialisation and parsing should be symmetric: a round-trip test catches formatting bugs
If any field could contain the delimiter, use proper CSV quoting and escaping
The mapping function is one-to-one: each Employee becomes exactly one CSV line
For file output, write the list with Files.write or BufferedWriter after collecting

s1_definition.oneliner: `map` can serialise each object into a CSV row by joining its fields with commas.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Serialising map**: turns each `Employee` back into a single comma-separated string.
- **`toPlainString()`** on BigDecimal avoids scientific notation for very large numbers.
- **Round-trip symmetry**: parse then serialise should reproduce the original line, and vice versa.
- **Escaping**: if a field could contain the delimiter, use proper CSV quoting or a library.
- **File output**: collect the CSV lines into a list, then write with `Files.write()` or `BufferedWriter`.
s1_definition.analogy: The clerk at the National Bank of India now has filled employee forms and must send them back out as plain text, one line per person like "Rajesh,Loans,95000". She reads each form and writes its fields on a line separated by commas.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Employee("Rajesh", "Loans", 95000)
       │
       │  map(e -> name + "," + dept + "," + salary.toPlainString())
       ▼
  String: "Rajesh,Loans,95000"

  Employee("Priya", "IT", 120000)
       │
       │  map(e -> ...)
       ▼
  String: "Priya,IT,120000"

  Collected → List<String>
  ["Rajesh,Loans,95000", "Priya,IT,120000", "Amit,Finance,85000"]
       │
       │  Files.write(path, lines)
       ▼
  employees.csv on disk
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To serialise structured objects back into CSV I use a map whose function joins each object's fields with commas, so the stream goes from employees to strings, one row per employee. For the salary I render it with `toPlainString()` so the output never slips into scientific notation.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India this was the nightly export to a partner system that only accepts plain CSV. It is the exact reverse of the import.

The most important quality check is the round-trip test: parsing a line and serialising it again should reproduce the original, and serialising an object and parsing it back should reproduce the original object. For data that is not guaranteed delimiter-free I use a proper CSV library for quoting and escaping.

Remember one sentence: `map(e -> name + "," + dept + "," + salary.toPlainString())` serialises each employee to a CSV row, and a round-trip test verifies correctness.
